question: Does the cached speculative implementation deliver a wall-clock speedup when draft and target are the same model?

setup.kv_cache: enabled on BOTH draft and target
setup.baseline: plain target generation WITH KV cache (the honest baseline)

conclusion: NEGATIVE, and expected. At zero gap every proposal is accepted (100%), so no target forward pass is saved, but each round still costs 2*K draft/target forwards instead of K plain forwards. Speedup 0.41-0.50x: roughly 2x SLOWER than plain cached generation. Zero gap is the worst possible configuration and exists only to prove correctness.

bug_found_and_fixed.symptom: acceptance was 15-40% at zero gap where it must be 100%
bug_found_and_fixed.cause: the draft loop and the target verification loop re-fed the ENTIRE sequence on top of an already-prefilled KV cache, double-counting the context; target p therefore differed from draft q even for identical weights
bug_found_and_fixed.fix: strict cache invariant - at the top of each round the cache holds exactly the accepted sequence and the held base logits predict the position after it; every inner forward feeds only new tokens

not_yet_measured: speedup and acceptance at a real model gap (1.5M -> 2.6M -> 6.3M); the zero-gap number is a correctness proof, not a performance result
